name: Honey Locust

facts.how: Pulp eaten raw or dried and ground

caution: Eat the sweet pulp, not the hard seeds. Do not confuse with the toxic black locust: honey locust has long twisted pods with sweet pulp and fierce branched thorns. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Foot-long twisting brown pods and, on wild trees, alarming branched thorns. Inside the pods is a sticky sweet pulp.

sections.title: In the kitchen
sections.body: The honey-sweet pulp can be scraped and eaten or dried and ground into a sweetener, much like mesquite.
